chunks: And it was narrated from Hāshim al-Ḥannāṭ that he said: I heard Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام saying:
"Whatever eats leaves and trees, there is no problem in praying in it; and whatever eats carrion, then do not pray in it."

key_terms.الشَّجَرَ: trees or vegetation, referring to herbivorous feeding
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةَ: carrion, the flesh of dead animals not lawfully slaughtered
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or objection

ai.seo_question: Which animal-derived garments are permissible to wear in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for garments used in salat (prayer), distinguishing between animals that feed on vegetation and those that feed on carrion. It indicates the permissibility of praying in what comes from herbivorous animals and the impermissibility of praying in what comes from carrion-eating animals.
